summary: prof.kaya@aegean.edu shows 10 Portugal sign-ins via university VPN vpn-edge-02 (F4). VPN appliance vpn-edge-01 (firmware 22.7R2.3) is listed in CISA KEV and suspected of external access (F7). Rejected impossible-travel, token-replay, shared-ASN, and password-spray claims were explained as non-interactive mail sync or organisational egress. Risk Gate directs escalation at confidence 0.6.

risk.rationale: All account-level suspicious claims for prof.kaya@aegean.edu were rejected with substantive criticism: the Turkey events are non-interactive ExchangeSync/15 mail-sync tokens (not interactive sign-ins or session replays); the 193.140.10.21 ASN is the organisation's shared egress/NAT with 202 distinct accounts completing MFA (threshold 10), so cross-account failures are background noise, not a spray; and the VPN actually used for the user's sign-ins is vpn-edge-02 (firmware 22.7R2.8, patched) from managed device LT-3104 in PT — not the flagged vpn-edge-01. Verified findings are non-confirmatory: F4 is only LIKELY (PT sign-ins via managed VPN device, consistent with legitimate use), and F7 is SUSPECTED (not confirmed), concerns vpn-edge-01 rather than the appliance in use, and lists KEV CVEs without evidence of exploitation or takeover. No confirmed account-takeover chain and no data-quality conflicts; the suspicious signals are explained away.
